simple.meaning: שָׁחַק (shâchaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to comminate (by trituration or attrition).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Exodus, 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, beginning at Exodus 30:36. Its contexts include covenant.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁחַק (H7833).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

firstOccurrence.englishText: You shall beat some of it very small, and put some of it before the covenant in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be to you most holy.

timeline.evidenceText: You shall beat some of it very small, and put some of it before the covenant in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be to you most holy.
Then I beat them as small as the dust of the earth.
You have delivered me from the strivings of the people.

definitions.full: H7833. shachaq [ שָׁחַק ] verb rub away, beat fine, pulverize (so Arabic , worn garment, thin clouds ; Aramaic שְׁחַק , pilverize ; Ecclus שחק Ecclesiasticus 6:36 is go often (wear by treading), Str compare iter terere ); — Qal Perfect 3plural מַיִם שָֽׁחֲקוּ אֲבָּנִים Job 14:19 waters rub away stones ; 2 masculine singular וְשָׁחַקְתָּ֫ Exod 30:36 (P; of pulverizing incense, see דקק Hiph`il ); figurative, accusative of foes, Imperfect 1singular suffix וְאֶשְׁחָקֵם 2Sam 22:43 (||) = Psa 18:43 .
